findings.title: Unconditional access to organization_context.member attribute can crash the endpoint
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated on every GET request to this endpoint, regardless of the `optimized_pagination` query parameter. If the requesting user is not a superuser, `organization_context.member` is accessed; for callers where `member` is `None` (e.g. a non-member caller permitted through some other path) this raises an `AttributeError`. Additionally, `has_global_access` does not appear to be an existing attribute on the organization member RPC model used elsewhere in the codebase, which would make this crash on every non-superuser request to the audit log endpoint, not just when the new optimized-pagination feature is requested. This turns what should be an opt-in feature into a potential 500 error for normal customer use of the audit log API.

findings.title: Unrelated, untested, privilege-gated pagination feature bundled into audit log endpoint
findings.body: This endpoint now branches into a brand-new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` code path based on a client-supplied `optimized_pagination` query parameter, gated only by `is_superuser`/`has_global_access`. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (spans buffer eviction), has no new tests covering the branch, and (per the related finding in paginator.py) the underlying negative-offset logic it enables is broken and will raise an exception at runtime. Shipping an untested, privilege-gated alternate code path with vague comments like "this is safe" inside an unrelated PR is risky and should be reviewed/tested on its own, or removed if unintentional.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch will raise an exception, not optimize anything
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`). Django QuerySets explicitly disallow negative slice indices and raise an exception (`AssertionError`/`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported`) in `QuerySet.__getitem__`. This means the newly-added "advanced" negative-offset pagination path is non-functional and will crash any request that reaches it (e.g. a superuser manually crafting a cursor string with a negative offset), rather than providing the described performance optimization.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator.get_result silently changed offset-clamping behavior for all paginated endpoints
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` modifies `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is the base class used by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator`, and other widely-used paginators across the whole codebase, not just the spans-buffer feature this PR is about. Previously, a negative cursor offset (e.g. from a tampered/corrupted cursor string) would fail loudly via Django's queryset slicing restriction; now it is silently clamped to 0 for forward cursors, changing pagination semantics without any accompanying tests or documentation of the new contract, and leaving the `is_prev` branch still able to pass a negative offset straight into queryset slicing (same crash risk as before, just for a different code path).

findings.title: Misleading comment claims negative-offset support with no corresponding behavior change
findings.body: The added comment states "Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios... This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions" directly above `self.offset = int(offset)`, which is unchanged code. No validation or new behavior was actually added here; the comment implies a capability that doesn't exist in this file and is misleading to future readers trying to understand where negative-offset support is implemented or guarded.

findings.title: Redirect-depth loop limit reduced 10x with explanatory comment removed
findings.body: The loop bound for walking the redirect chain was reduced from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000`, and the comment explaining the known correctness limitation ("theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted entirely rather than updated. This makes it 10x more likely in practice for deeply-nested span trees to hit the redirect-depth cutoff and be incorrectly merged/split, and removes the only documentation warning maintainers about this risk, with no explanation given for why the limit was lowered.

findings.title: zpopmin eviction can remove the segment's root span, corrupting flushed output
findings.body: When a segment's span count exceeds 1000, `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts the lowest-scored (oldest `end_timestamp_precise`) entries with no protection for the span that is the segment's root (`is_segment_span`). If the root span's end timestamp happens to be lower than one or more of its children's (e.g. due to clock skew or async child spans finishing later), the root span's payload can be evicted from the sorted set while the separate `has_root_span` boolean flag remains true. Later, `flush_segments` in buffer.py determines `is_segment` by comparing `segment_span_id == val["span_id"]` only over the spans actually present in the set; if the root span was evicted, no span in the flushed output will have `is_segment: true`, even though the segment was flushed via the root-span timeout path. This silently produces segments lacking a root span marker, which downstream consumers expecting exactly one root span per segment may not handle correctly.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now dead/disconnected from the actual eviction threshold
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans: int = 1001`, but nothing in the class uses this value anymore (the only prior usage, in `_load_segment_data`, was removed). The actual span-count cap enforced during insertion is now hardcoded as `1000` inside `add-buffer.lua` and is not derived from or passed through this configuration value. This leaves a misleading, non-functional configuration knob: changing `max_segment_spans` has no effect on behavior, and the real cap (1000) is off-by-one from the stated default (1001) and only discoverable by reading the Lua script.

findings.title: Removed oversized-segment safety check and metric with no replacement observability
findings.body: The previous check in `_load_segment_data` that dropped and logged (via `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded")` and `logger.error`) segments whose span count exceeded `max_segment_spans` was removed without any replacement. The new insertion-time eviction in `add-buffer.lua` silently trims excess spans via `zpopmin` and does not report whether/how many spans were evicted (the script's return tuple `{redirect_depth, span_key, set_key, has_root_span}` carries no eviction count), so there is no metric or log anywhere indicating that spans are being dropped from an oversized segment. This is a loss of operational visibility into data loss that previously existed.

findings.title: No test exercises the new insert-time span eviction behavior
findings.body: The PR's stated purpose is to add eviction during insert for the spans buffer (capping segments at 1000 spans via `zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua), but the only changes to this test file are adding the new required `end_timestamp_precise` field to existing `Span(...)` constructions. No test inserts more than 1000 spans into a single segment to verify that old spans are correctly evicted, that the segment is capped at the expected size, or that the root span survives eviction. The core new behavior introduced by this PR is therefore untested.

findings.title: No tests added for new OptimizedCursorPaginator class
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is a substantial new class (~90 lines) with a non-trivial negative-offset code path, but no test file changes accompany it in this PR. Given that the negative-offset branch appears to be broken (see related finding on queryset negative slicing), the absence of any unit test means this bug would not be caught before merging or in CI.
